title: Pregnancy scan, 2nd and 3rd trimester
what: An ultrasound of your baby in the second and third part of pregnancy. The doctor checks how the baby is growing, the baby's organs, the placenta, and the fluid.
why: Offered to all pregnant women: the second scan usually at 18 to 21 weeks, the third at about 30 to 34 weeks. Your doctor will tell you the exact timing.
tell_doctor: How many weeks pregnant you are, and your first scan results
If you are expecting twins or the pregnancy is after IVF
If you have had discharge, pain, or changes in the baby's movements

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special prep needed. A full bladder is usually not needed at this stage.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can eat as usual. Do not come hungry.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable so your belly is easy to uncover.

bring: Results of past scans and ultrasounds
steps: You lie on your back with your belly bare
The doctor puts on gel and looks at the baby through your belly
The baby's growth is measured and the organs are checked
The placenta, the amount of fluid, and the cervix are checked
At the third scan, blood flow is often checked. This is called Doppler
feel: It does not hurt. You feel the probe pressing
If you feel dizzy or sick lying on your back, say so. You will be turned onto your side
You may see your baby on the screen
after: You usually get the report right away
If something needs a closer look, the doctor will tell you which tests you need
red_flags: Bleeding, leaking fluid, or severe belly pain: call emergency services
The baby is moving much less than usual: see a doctor right away
A severe headache, spots before your eyes, or a swollen face: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I find out the baby's sex at the second scan?
faq.a: Usually yes, if the baby is lying in a good position. But the main goal is to check how the baby is developing.

faq.q: Why have a third scan if the second one was fine?
faq.a: Near the end of pregnancy, it matters how the baby is growing, how the placenta is working, and how the baby is lying before birth.

reminders.text: Pregnancy scan tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record and past ultrasounds.
